questions.q: P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2. Find P(A ∪ B).
questions.why: P(A ∪ B) = 0.4 + 0.5 − 0.2 = 0.7; 0.9 forgets to subtract the overlap.

questions.q: P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.6 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.18. Which statement is true?
options: A and B are mutually exclusive
A and B are mutually exclusive and independent
A and B are independent but not mutually exclusive
questions.why: 0.3 × 0.6 = 0.18 = P(A ∩ B), so independent; P(A ∩ B) ≠ 0, so not mutually exclusive.
